nodes.summary: The k-MEDIAN decision problem. k-MEDIAN (generalized, nonmetric) is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a k-median instance $(d, K, B)$ that is well formed and feasible. That is, $d$ has rows $d_0, \dots, d_{n-1}$ (the clients) of a common length $m$ (the locations), and there are a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ of at most $K$…
nodes.title: The k-MEDIAN decision problem

nodes.summary: The k-MEDIAN decision problem is in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: k-MEDIAN (GENERALIZED, NONMETRIC) is NP-complete

nodes.summary: Let $(d, K, B)$ be a k-median instance whose cost matrix $d$ has rows $d_0, \dots, d_{n-1}$, one per client, and let $m$ be the length of $d_0$, or $m = 0$ when $n = 0$. The instance is feasible when there are a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ of at most $K$ locations and a choice of $a(c) \in S$ for each client $c < n$ such that $\sum_{c < n} d_c(a(c)) \le B$, where $d_c(j)$ is the entry of $d_c$ at index $j$…
nodes.title: Feasible k-median instances

nodes.summary: A k-median instance is a triple $(d, K, B)$ of a cost matrix $d$, given as a list of rows of natural numbers (one row per client, one entry per location; the rows need not have equal length), a natural number $K$ bounding the number of open locations, and a natural-number budget $B$.
nodes.title: k-median instances

nodes.summary: A k-median instance $(d, K, B)$ is well formed when all rows of its cost matrix $d$ have the same length.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
